Title: Five Layers to Better Personalization — How we built an LLM-powered profile stack for 500M+ Edge users

The problem
For years our personalization relied on a few flat signals (last-click, coarse categories, and sparse behavior logs). That produced stale, brittle profiles that missed short-term interests and couldn’t represent nuance in behavior from the browser. We needed richer, temporally-aware profiles that could scale to hundreds of millions of users without adding visible latency.

What we built (overview)
We shipped a 5-layer, LLM-driven profile system that turns Edge behavioral signals into compact, actionable user profiles. The architecture separates user characteristics by stability and use-case so we can update frequently where it matters, cache aggressively where it doesn’t, and serve everything under tight latency SLAs. The system processes signals for 500M+ daily active users and serves profiles at P99 < 5 ms.

The five layers (plain language)
- L1 — Identity: Core, rarely-changing facts (age bracket, general region, language). Small, strongly validated items that are paged rarely and used for baseline targeting and safety checks.
- L2 — Stable Preferences: Things like long-term topical interests and affinities that evolve on a weekly cadence. These are recomputed periodically so downstream systems have consistent signals without reacting to noise.
- L3 — Dynamic Interests: Short-term signals derived from browser behavior (recent tabs, time-on-page patterns, topical engagement). Updated daily, this layer captures what a user is actively exploring now.
- L4 — World Context: Global and regional context such as trending events, seasonality (holidays, sports), and breaking news that temporarily re-weights relevance. We compute this once per epoch and make it available to enrich L2/L3 without reprocessing raw signals.
- L5 — Interest Cards: Triggered, hyper-personalized micro-profiles generated on demand for specific surfaces (e.g., a promoted story card, an ad slot). These are created with on-the-fly LLM elicitation using L1–L4 as context and are intentionally ephemeral.

How the pieces fit together
We use a two-path inference strategy. The background pipeline continuously updates L1–L4 and stores compact embeddings and metadata. At request time, lightweight routing fetches the relevant layers and, when needed, invokes a succinct LLM prompt to produce an L5 Interest Card. Because L1–L4 are cached and coarse-grained, the LLM sees a small, informative context window — this keeps runtime cost down and tail latency under our targets. All Edge-derived signals are ingested with privacy-preserving aggregation and opt-in handling; sensitive fields are anonymized before modelization.

Performance and impact (selected metrics)
- Scale: processes signals for 500M+ daily active users; supports peak serving at ~20k QPS.
- Latency: P99 profile serve time < 5 ms (avg ~1.1 ms, P50 ~0.6 ms).
- Relevance: click-through rate (CTR) on personalized units improved by 11% overall (14% in high-intent cohorts).
- Business: estimated incremental revenue lift of ~4.2% on targeted inventory in the first 8 weeks.
- Efficiency: inference cost per high-value personalization reduced by ~30% versus our prior monolithic model through layered caching and targeted LLM calls.

Team callouts
- Maya (Lead ML Engineer) designed the prompting strategy and the L4 contextualizer that lets the model respect both global trends and individual signals.
- Carlos (Infra Engineering) led the serving redesign and load testing that gave us the P99 < 5 ms guarantee at global scale.
- Priya (Privacy & Data) implemented the opt-in pipeline, anonymization layers, and audit tooling so we could use Edge signals safely and transparently.
- Ethan (Product Manager) coordinated cross-org telemetry and the rollout plan that let us validate impact incrementally and iterate fast.

What’s next
- Make L5 Interest Cards multi-modal (incorporate thumbnails and short video previews) while preserving our latency targets.
- Improve personalization fairness by adding counterfactual evaluation and group-level performance dashboards.
- Continue optimizing cost with adaptive model sizes for different surfaces and user segments.

Closing
This release represents a pragmatic blend of LLM capability and systems engineering: we got better personalization by decomposing the problem into layers, shipping conservative defaults first, and adding targeted LLM generation only where it moves the needle. Big thanks to everyone on Ads Personalization and our cross-functional partners — excited for the next iteration.
